newsitem.title: UK: UK group seeks to shield consumers from junk email.
newsitem.headline: UK group seeks to shield consumers from junk email.

text.p: Britain's Direct Marketing Association (DMA) said on Wednesday it was looking for partners to help launch a service to protect consumers from unwanted electronic "junk mail".

It said the service would shield Internet users from unsolicited marketing emails -- known in the computer world as "spams" -- in the same way it says it helps consumers avoid getting unwanted marketing phone calls and mailings.
A growing number of companies are using email to send computer users press releases, information on new products and services, and other promotional material.
DMA said it wanted partners to help it create an E-Mail Preference Service (EPS), which would be similar to existing "Mailing Preference Service and Telephone Preference" schemes.
These two programmes, which are part of the British direct marketing industry's self-regulatory framework, allow customers to choose to not receive unsolicited marketing phone calls and mailings.

"We need associate partners for the first two years of operation to set up the scheme," Trevor Richer, chairman of the DMA's E-Mail Preference Service Working Party, said in a statement. "After the initial two years the EPS should be self-supporting."
